title: How Alien Contact Might Work
summary: Josh and Chuck take a freewheeling look at how alien contact might work. They cover primitive life versus intelligent life discoveries, including the ALH84001 Mars meteorite; SETI and the International Academy of Astronautics protocols; the Rio scale for rating public excitement (proposed 2000 by Yvonne Almar and Jill Tarter, updated as Rio 2.0 in 2018 by Duncan Forgan); the Great Filter; the 1950s "Seven Steps to Contact" document; SETA (search for extraterrestrial artifacts) and the three artifact classes; 'Oumuamua and Avi Loeb's Galileo Project; the UAP report; Lincos, a language designed by Hans Freudenthal; xenolinguistics; the risks of advanced civilizations being selfish or universalist; and the X-factor risks in the World Economic Forum report. The episode ends with a plug for the hosts' End of the World with Josh Clark podcast and a listener mail about word usage.
topics: World Economic Forum global risks X factors

entities.name: End of the World with Josh Clark
Close Encounters of the Third Kind

segments.title: Opening banter and framing
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with off-topic banter, a plug for the board game on Amazon, and a preview that the episode will be freewheeling. They frame the topic as humanity's loosely planned approach to possibly communicating with aliens, and note that some researchers are working on it without much government funding.

segments.title: Primitive life versus intelligent life
segments.summary: They distinguish discovery of primitive life from contact with intelligent life. They discuss NASA's planned response to microbial life on Mars and the ALH84001 meteorite, which contains circumstantial evidence of ancient microbial life but is still debated. They introduce the term ETI.

segments.title: Challenges of communicating and science fiction influence
segments.summary: They note that we do not know what alien intelligence would look like or whether it could process communication. They discuss the influence of science fiction on ideas about aliens and how science fiction writers have made accurate predictions.
topics: science fiction influence on alien contact

segments.title: Seven Steps to Contact and the probe rule of thumb
segments.summary: Avi Loeb-era thinking aside, they cite Jacob Haqq-Misra of Penn State, who suggests observing alien intelligence from a distance before approaching. They describe the reportedly 1950s military document Seven Steps to Contact. They describe a rule of thumb that advanced civilizations may already have used the methods humans would choose, such as space probes.

segments.title: The Great Filter and advanced civilizations
segments.summary: They explain the Great Filter idea: advanced civilizations would have survived technological dangers. They discuss whether humanity is near the filter and whether contact with an advanced civilization would show that the filter is behind us.

segments.title: Aliens may already be watching Earth
segments.summary: They note that aliens may already be observing Earth, likely through a probe, possibly hidden in a co-orbital asteroid. They joke about Han Solo and mining asteroids.

segments.title: SETI protocols and the IAA guidelines
segments.summary: They discuss the SETI episode reference and the International Academy of Astronautics, a non-governmental body founded in 1960 with member countries, which established protocols in the late 1980s and updated them later. The guidelines stress honesty, transparency with the press, international collaboration, and not responding hastily.

segments.title: The Rio scale
segments.summary: They explain the Rio scale, a zero-to-ten scale proposed in 2000 by Yvonne Almar and Jill Tarter to gauge how excited the public should be about a discovery, modeled on the Torino scale. They describe examples, and Rio 2.0 updated in 2018 under Duncan Forgan of the University of St Andrews. A dad joke about 'she dances on the sand' closes the segment.

segments.title: Selfish or universalist aliens and motives
segments.summary: They discuss whether aliens would be selfish or universalist, possible reasons to harm humans such as resources or eliminating rivals, the possibility of accidental infection, and the idea that long-lived civilizations are likely cooperative. They compare contact to historical colonial encounters and to the transmission of lost Greek knowledge to Europe.

segments.title: SETA, artifacts, and 'Oumuamua
segments.summary: They define SETA as the search for extraterrestrial artifacts and describe three classes of artifacts proposed by Robert Freitas Jr. and Francisco Valdes. They discuss 'Oumuamua, Avi Loeb's view that it may be alien technology, and the Galileo Project and the UAP report from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

segments.title: Communicating with aliens: Lincos and xenolinguistics
segments.summary: They discuss the difficulty of communicating with an unfamiliar intelligence. They cover Hans Freudenthal's Lincos, a designed radio-based language of math and science symbols, and the field of xenolinguistics. They note the vast distances involved, with Carl Sagan's observation that communication can take generations.

segments.title: Global risk and X factors
segments.summary: They describe a white paper led by Katherine Denning and Stephen Dick calling for more funding, citing the World Economic Forum's X factors, including contact with extraterrestrial life, climate change, cognitive enhancement, geoengineering, and longer lifespans.

segments.title: Plug for End of the World with Josh Clark
segments.summary: Chuck plugs Josh's ten-part series End of the World with Josh Clark, and they joke about a possible TV adaptation.
topics: End of the World with Josh Clark

segments.title: Listener mail about word usage
segments.summary: A listener writes to correct 'quashed' versus 'squashed' from a Free Press episode and to point out that 'contemporaneous' is the right word instead of 'contemporary' for articles from the same period. The hosts accept the corrections.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close with a call for listener email and the show credits.
